source.title: Discovering Interpretable Biological Concepts in Single-cell RNA-seq Foundation Models
source.authors: C. Claye; P. Marschall; Wassila Ouerdane; Céline Hudelot; Julien Duquesne

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure and table content has extraction/layout artifacts, but the relevant reported results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies sparse autoencoders to scRNA-seq foundation-model embeddings and reports results on concept stability and preservation of downstream signal in this new model setting. It does not test toy-model superposition itself.
record.gate_note: The study tests cross-dataset stability of SAE concepts and compares downstream prediction from concept versus neuron activations, which bear on V5's stability and signal-preservation aspects. It does not measure superposition geometry, capacity competition, or whether the concepts are canonical units. Results cited from other papers are not included. SAE scale results used to choose hyperparameters are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Trains Top-k SAEs on scRNA-seq foundation models (scVI, scGPT) and measures cross-dataset stability of SAE concepts. This bears on V5's stability claim in a new, non-LLM setting. It does not test superposition geometry, capacity, polysemanticity causes or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Authors conclude SAE concepts are more interpretable than neurons and preserve biological signal. They also report that some concepts are stable across datasets, and that richer prior knowledge could aid interpretation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Topk sparse autoencoders on scRNA-seq model embeddings and evaluates biological interpretation, cross-dataset matching, and downstream classification; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Stability differs by model: the authors report greater cross-dataset stability for scVI concepts than for scGPT concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: In a blinded expert study and in pathway enrichment, SAE concepts were more interpretable than individual neurons for both models. Nearly half of the concepts remained uninterpretable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features are more monosemantic/interpretable than neurons in non-LLM (biological) foundation models.

fits_no_version.finding: Logistic regression on concept activations matches neuron activations (0.86 vs 0.87 cell type; 0.49 vs 0.48 cell cycle).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE concept bases preserve linearly decodable task signal of the original representation.

record.problems: Cross-dataset stability is assessed across two datasets, not across random seeds; the paper reports selected matched examples and a qualitative model comparison without aggregate stability values in the text. Downstream preservation is evaluated on only two classification tasks. The study does not establish completeness or canonical status of the SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version rows were left out. SAE scale and reconstruction results in Section 4.2/Figure 2 were used in part to select hyperparameters and do not test the claim versions.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity transition, geometry: not studied.
Capacity competition as cause of polysemanticity: not studied.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity: not studied.
Not LLMs. SAE recovery of sparse features is shown only in scRNA-seq models.
Seed stability, canonicity across dictionary sizes, and completeness beyond reconstruction R2 were not tested.

missing.what: Cross-dataset reconstruction R2: slightly lower on the test dataset for all SAEs, with a larger drop for scGPT. This indicates dataset-specific concepts are missing from each dictionary.
Aggregate Hungarian-matched cosine similarity per SAE scale for both models (the actual stability measure); not readable in the extracted text.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Stability is tested across datasets only, not seeds. Both dataset gene-vocabulary mismatches (scVI 3896/8000 genes matched; scGPT 250 shared genes) confound the stability comparison. The rows r1-r3 are illustrative high-cosine picks and cannot support general stability.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemantic neurons or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity and whether it is evidence of superposition.
The models studied are scRNA-seq foundation models, not LLMs; the study does not measure feature spread across neurons in LLMs.

The study measures cross-dataset concept stability and signal preservation on two classification tasks, but does not establish that SAE features are canonical units or complete across the model's representation.
Whether features are one-dimensional directions or have multi-dimensional geometry.

rows.subject: scVI
rows.operation_detail: Matched concept-vector cosine similarity across SAEs trained on two datasets

conditions.value: Tabula Sapiens Immune and Cross-Tissue Immune Cell Atlas

rows.measure: Cosine similarity of matched concept vectors
rows.note: The example concepts are both interpreted as heat-shock protein response; the paper describes the examples as high-cosine matches.
rows.check: Selected example: the paper explicitly picks pairs 'with a high cosine similarity' for illustration. This value describes a chosen match, not dictionary-level stability, so it should not be used as evidence of general stability.

rows.subject: scGPT
rows.operation_detail: Matched concept-vector cosine similarity across SAEs trained on two datasets

conditions.value: Tabula Sapiens Immune and Cross-Tissue Immune Cell Atlas

rows.measure: Cosine similarity of matched concept vectors
rows.note: Both concepts are interpreted as response to interferon signalling.
rows.check: Selected high-cosine example pair, not an aggregate stability measure. Same caveat as r1.

rows.subject: scGPT
rows.operation_detail: Matched concept-vector cosine similarity across SAEs trained on two datasets

conditions.value: Tabula Sapiens Immune and Cross-Tissue Immune Cell Atlas

rows.measure: Cosine similarity of matched concept vectors
rows.note: The paper notes that this pair has no top-10 genes in common, although the genes belong to the same family.
rows.check: Selected example pair, not an aggregate measure. Note the pair shares no top-10 genes despite 0.84 cosine.

rows.subject: scVI
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-dataset alignment of matched concept vectors

conditions.value: Tabula Sapiens Immune and Cross-Tissue Immune Cell Atlas

rows.measure: Relative stability of matched concepts, assessed by cosine similarity
rows.baseline: scGPT concepts trained on the same two datasets
rows.value: The authors report that concepts extracted from scVI embeddings are more stable than those from scGPT.
rows.note: The paper reports a model-level comparison but gives no aggregate numerical stability value in the text.
rows.check: Fig 4.B gives the aggregate matched cosine per scale, but values are unreadable in the extracted text. The authors frame it as 'some concepts are stable'. The comparison is confounded: only 3896/8000 scVI genes matched in the Cross-Tissue atlas.

rows.subject: scGPT
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-dataset alignment of matched concept vectors

conditions.value: Tabula Sapiens Immune and Cross-Tissue Immune Cell Atlas

rows.measure: Relative stability of matched concepts, assessed by cosine similarity
rows.baseline: scVI concepts trained on the same two datasets
rows.value: The authors report that scGPT concepts are less stable than scVI concepts.
rows.note: The paper reports a model-level comparison but gives no aggregate numerical stability value in the text.
rows.check: Lower stability for scGPT. The authors link this to only 250 shared input genes between the datasets, a confound rather than a property of the SAE.

rows.subject: scGPT
rows.operation_detail: Compared logistic-regression classification using concept activations with classification using neuron activations
rows.note: The authors describe the accuracies as similar, indicating preservation of signal for this task.
rows.check: Downstream accuracy of concept vs neuron activations measures linear signal preservation. It does not measure completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

rows.subject: scGPT
rows.operation_detail: Compared logistic-regression classification using concept activations with classification using neuron activations

conditions.value: Cell cycle phase classification; G1, S, and G2M

rows.note: The authors describe the accuracies as similar, indicating preservation of signal for this task.
rows.check: Same as r6. Near-chance-level task accuracy (0.48/0.49) for both concepts and neurons.

relationships.condition: Cross-dataset SAE stability, scVI and scGPT on two immune-cell datasets
relationships.reason: Authors report only 'some concepts are stable', with stability lower for scGPT than scVI and cross-dataset R2 dropping, so dictionaries are not identical across data (r4, r5; R2 drop from text Fig 4.A).
relationships.display_finding: The authors report only that some concepts are stable, with lower stability for scGPT than scVI and a drop in cross-dataset R², so the dictionaries were not identical across data.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The reported matched-concept examples and the two downstream classification tasks
reader_labels.reason: The example pairs have reported cosine similarities of 0.84–0.95, and concept activations achieve accuracy similar to neuron activations on both tasks (r1-r3, r6-r7). These results support stability for selected matches and preservation of signal on the tested tasks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-dataset stability comparison across the studied models
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that only some concepts are stable and that scVI concepts are more stable than scGPT concepts; the results therefore do not establish general stability across all concepts or models (r4-r5).
